posts.name: arenson9
posts.cooked:
Eleven people at Arsenal tonight. And they had a new brisket sandwhich which was absolutely delicious, if a bit on the small side.

 

TheJayMann has a new job folks. I am very impressed at the position he got and he seems delighted with it. Kudos to you, Jeff. Also kudos to you for organizing a few people to share transport to STL for the upcoming Vengeance release party.

 

Koga showed up and brought with him not only printed decks of the final proofs from the Vengeance playtester forum and printed decks of his own custom heroes, etc., but a whole slew of custom decks from a particular person (don't know the handle/name) on BGG. My table had a great game (a win!) against the Matriarch and then elected to try out these custom decks and had a lot of fun with the mystery of just what the heck would turn up. Are they well-balanced? Dunno. Just played with them once, but it was fun, despite losing.

 

AND, the decks were absolutely beautiful -- both Koga's and the ones from BGG. They looked very much in the same style as Adam's art and Koga spent the time and the money to print them on very nice cards. He even made up custom dividers. At a glance, for instance, with the Vengenace decks mixed into his game boxes with all the other decks, it looked like he'd somehow gotten an early version rather than printing it himself.

 

There were a couple of people there I hadn't met before and still didn't meet, friends of imprimis5. Looking forward to sharing a table with you all at some point in the future. 

 

And I did not ride my bike. Sadly, I am becoming a sloth. I let the single digit temps and likelihood of snow and ice on the road dissuade me. Next time, maybe.

Good time at Comic Carnival today. We had five people, despite the absence of a few of our regulars. A special welcome again to Blue Kae. Very nice to see you there. Sorry I was a bit protective of my cards. I'm like that.

 

We played one five player game with the new heroes against The Ennead in the Freedom Five Tower. It looked rough at first, but some deck manipulation and luck kept any other of the Ennead from joining the original five and we were able to handle them fairly easily.

 

We then played a four player game against the Vengeful Five (minus Proletariat) in the MDP. GI Legacy and Tempest with the Grievous Hailstorm were a killer combo, combining for six damage to every non-villain target every round. A couple of the heroes got pretty close to zero, but all in all a pretty comfortable victory.

 

After my initial playtests of the V5 I was fairly pessimistic that I would ever really enjoy playing against them -- too complicated and too time consuming. Turns out, though, that once you are familiar with them (like all new decks, duh) if you have a little extra time and are playing with people who are comfortable running a villain, it's super fun.

 

Quite unintentionally, The Ennead proved to be a lovely segue into a V5 game, since they have multiple villain character cards with incapacitated powers.

 

And I bought the Firefly game when I saw it at the store because FIREFLY! ... and it also came with bonus pieces for playing with a fifth ship.
